result.title: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
result.summary: GUI agents built on large language and vision-language models still struggle on unseen applications and complex multi-step tasks, as completing real GUI tasks depends on app-specific, temporally volatile operational knowledge that is scarce in pretraining corpora. Retrieval-augmented execution offers a natural remedy but faces two coupled bottlenecks: knowledge at scale is hard to acquire, and self-collected priors inevitably drift from the live environment due to version updates, promotions, ads, A/B tests, and personalization. We therefore argue that GUI agents should not pursue perfect knowledge but learn to act correctly under imperfect priors, and propose our framework that couples knowledge acquisition with noise-robust utilization: a structured exploration strategy traverses interactive elements, builds a UI state-transition graph, and synthesizes (task, trajectory) pairs via a VLM without human annotation; a noise-aware training strategy, grounded in a taxonomy of real GUI drift patterns, injects five types of realistic errors into self-explored trajectories to teach the agent to assess prior reliability before acting. Experiments on physical devices and online emulator benchmarks show that our method discovers more unique screens, covers more benchmark tasks, and more effectively rejects erroneous priors while leveraging correct ones, with accuracy gains that transfer across datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向 GUI agent 在未见应用与多步任务上的执行难题，提出不追求完美知识、而是在「不完美先验」下行动：用结构化探索遍历交互元素并构建 UI 状态转移图来合成 (任务, 轨迹) 数据，再按真实 GUI 漂移模式向自采轨迹注入五类错误，训练 agent 先评估先验可靠性再行动。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接状态生成关系，但「先评估先验可靠性再决定是否使用」的思路可能可供核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的证据筛选与停止决策，以及不可靠观测下的信念更新。
